heading: EXT. FROZEN LAKE - ICE FISHING DERBY - DAWN

units.text: EXT. FROZEN LAKE - ICE FISHING DERBY - DAWN
A white plain stitched with augered holes and plywood shanties.
Orange flags snap in the wind.
Hundreds of numbered bibs bob across the ice like pumpkins.
BRYNJA THORSDOTTIR, 50s, leathery, parka patched with duct tape, stands over hole 117, line taut in her hands.
Opposite her, OTTO WESTERBERG, 30s, new coat, a brand new rod, cheeks pink as ham, stands at hole 118 and has not yet felt a bite.
A loudspeaker crackles.
The derby ends in four minutes.
Your line moved.
units.name: OTTO

units.text: Wind.
units.name: BRYNJA

units.text: Mine moved.
units.name: OTTO

units.text: Also wind.
units.name: BRYNJA

units.text: They both jerk.
Lines go taut at the same instant.
Bobbers vanish.
Walleye!
units.name: OTTO

units.text: Pike!
units.name: BRYNJA

units.text: They haul in, side by side, boots scraping, grunts overlapping.
Two lines, two fish, both fighting, tangled in the middle of the hole.
Don't you dare cut me, Westerberg!
units.name: BRYNJA

units.text: Don't you dare let go, Thorsdottir!
units.name: OTTO

units.text: Pull!
units.name: OTTO

units.text: Pull!
units.name: BRYNJA

units.text: A great grey pike and a fat golden walleye burst from the same hole, flopping on the ice between them.
Both stand, panting.
The pike is longer.
The walleye is thicker.
The loudspeaker blares the final minute.
They stare at each other.
Then, together, they scoop up both fish and run.
